events.title: Proximity Exhibition

venue.name: Snug Harbor Cultural Center
venue.address: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C)

events.description: Discover PROXIMITY, featuring 10 Snug Harbor studio artists across painting, photography & mixed media. Explore how shared spaces and creative con
events.details: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor's longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place-it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another. events.title: The Art of Noticing: A Mindful Birding Experience
events.description: Explore how mindfulness can deepen our awareness, observation, and enjoyment of the natural world.
events.details: Join nature educator Ryan Mandelbaum and yoga/mindfulness instructor Susie Caramanica to explore how mindfulness can deepen our awareness, observation, and enjoyment of the natural world. This guided experience combines mindfulness practices with birding, inviting participants to slow down, clear mental distractions, and become more fully attentive to the environment around them. Through simple grounding exercises, participants will cultivate a focused awareness that can help them notice more-from a bird's song to subtle movement in the canopy, participants can fully appreciate an encounter that might otherwise go unnoticed. The program begins with gentle mindfulness practices designed to settle the mind and sharpen sensory awareness. Participants will then be guided through the landscape, learning to identify birds by sight and sound while observing behavior, habitat, migration, and seasonal activity. events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located in Tottenville on Staten Island
events.details: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies. Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp's great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance. It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution.
